functions.name: cp6TimeoutFire
functions.notes: Lazily initialises the timer registry, hashes the id into a bucket, walks the chain matching hash+id, invokes the callback through vtable slot 6, re-looks up after the callback, unlinks the node, decrements the live count, destroys the callback via slot 4/5 and frees entry+node. Trap behaviour matches for null callbacks and out-of-bounds pointers.

validation.comparison: Eleven registry scenarios: empty, absent key, power-of-two hit, non-power small id, collision, next-node rehash, duplicate id, self-based callback, null callback trap, lazy initialization and out-of-bounds bucket array. Each compares outcome/error constructor and message, complete 67,108,864-byte memory and the stack pointer.
limitations: A callback that mutates or rehashes the registry between invocation and removal is implemented but not differentially exercised.
A chain node equal to the sentinel, node+12==0 and out-of-bounds chain-node pointers are not exercised.
free 14, guard 31/32 and abort 42 remain native dependencies.
Ledger: 208 server bodies recovered and 526 remain machine code.
